points.description: States that array elements can be accessed directly (random/direct access by index, i.e. constant-time access to any element without traversing other elements).
points.partial_credit: Half if it says access is fast/by index but does not say it is direct or without traversal.

points.description: States that linked lists, by contrast, require iterative traversal (stepping node by node from the head) to reach an element.
points.partial_credit: Half if it only says linked lists are slower to access, without naming traversal.

points.description: Correctly makes the distinction in the right direction: the advantage is element access (direct vs sequential traversal), not insertion/deletion, memory use or size flexibility, and no wrong claim is made.

rubric.notes: Full marks need the precise fact: arrays give direct (index-based) access, whereas linked lists need iterative traversal. Vague wording such as "arrays are faster" or "easier to use" earns nothing for that point. Naming a wrong advantage (e.g. easier insertion, dynamic size) as the main one loses P3 and likely P1.
